## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to reason about 128-bit layout, edge cases, and using 64-bit intrinsics for performance.

## Key Concepts
- 128-bit value as hi/lo halves
- Most significant set bit index calculation
- Handling zero input

## Code Example
```c
int highestSetBitIndex128(uint128 x) {
  if (x.hi) return 64 + (63 - __builtin_clzll(x.hi));
  if (x.lo) return (63 - __builtin_clzll(x.lo));
  return -1;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to implement without builtins?
- Extend to 256-bit type?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of 128-bit rotation, edge-case handling without branches, and safe shift magnitudes using masking.

## Key Concepts

- Bitwise rotate with shifts
- Modulo-like normalization using masks
- Safe 128-bit shifts without UB

## Code Example

```cpp
uint128 ror128(uint128 x, unsigned int k) {
  k &= 127;
  return (x >> k) | (x << ((128 - k) & 127));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this with random k values and ensure no UB?
- How would you adapt for left-rotation and mixed-width types?

questions.explanation:
This question tests bit manipulation without loops. Mask `0x55555555` (=0101... in binary) extracts even-position bits (0, 2, 4, ...), while `0xAAAAAAAA` (=1010... in binary) extracts odd-position bits (1, 3, 5, ...). The compression uses a parallel prefix technique: each stage combines adjacent bits via `(x | (x >> 1))`, then masks to keep only relevant pairs. Four repetitions shrink 32 bits down to 16. The odd bits are shifted right by 8 at the end to position them in the upper 16 bits.

Follow-up: For 64-bit input, repeat the algorithm on each 32-bit half, then combine the results.

## Why This Is Asked

- Bitwise shifts and wrap-around semantics

```javascript
function rotl32(n, k) {

}
```

- How would you implement rotate-right similarly?

## Why This Is Asked
Constant-time 128-bit comparison is core in cryptography and DB internals to avoid timing channels; probe understanding of lexicographic, boundary handling without branches.

## Key Concepts
- Branchless logic with masks
- Lexicographic 128-bit comparison
- Handling hi/lo boundaries in constant time

## Code Example
```javascript
typedef struct { uint64_t hi; uint64_t lo; } uint128;
static inline int8_t cmp128(uint128 a, uint128 b) {
```
